subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should canonical agents.delete permanently own removal of all agent-scoped scheduler jobs, and if so must that cleanup be durably retryable after the agent config commit?
rationale: This changes an existing destructive Gateway method, persistent ownership state, and scheduled-execution cleanup semantics; code review cannot choose that permanent security and product boundary while the RFC remains open.

options.title: Require durable canonical cleanup
options.body: Approve agents.delete as the owner only after scheduler cleanup can resume idempotently following partial post-commit failures.

options.title: Keep cleanup Claw-specific
options.body: Leave ordinary agents.delete unchanged and retain cron reconciliation inside the experimental Claw lifecycle until a shared deletion contract is designed.

options.title: Pause for the RFC
options.body: Hold this stack stage until the Claws RFC explicitly settles scheduler ownership, deletion ordering, and recovery semantics.

recommendation.title: Require durable canonical cleanup
recommendation.body: Approve agents.delete as the owner only after scheduler cleanup can resume idempotently following partial post-commit failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned reviewer has already reproduced the relevant failures and defined the canonical deletion boundary expected from this stack stage.
